text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 3.2% today, extending a four-day rally that has now gained roughly 10% since early November. The move follows Trump's statements that the Iran conflict is ending "fairly soon," which eased geopolitical risk premium in oil prices — Brent crude dipped below $90 a barrel on those comments. For a refiner like Marathon, lower oil prices directly improve profitability on the products they sell (gasoline and diesel), while refineries running at 95.2% utilization mean they're operating near full capacity to capture that margin.

The broader context matters too: even though midterm elections brought a "blue wave" that favored renewable energy investment, oil markets are pricing in near-term energy demand and geopolitical stability. Trump's de-escalation rhetoric on Iran, whether or not a lasting peace deal materializes, has shifted sentiment away from the higher oil prices that prevailed earlier in the week when tensions looked more acute.
